title: Word Subsets
description:
You are given two string arrays words1 and words2. A string b is a subset of string a if every letter in b occurs in a including multiplicity. For example, "wrr" is a subset of "warrior" but is not a subset of "world". A string a from words1 is universal if for every string b in words2, b is a subset of a. Return an array of all the universal strings in words1. Return the universal strings in their original words1 order.

## Examples

```text
Example 1
Input: words1 = ["amazon","apple","facebook","google","leetcode"], words2 = ["e","o"]
Output: ["facebook","google","leetcode"]
```

```text
Example 2
Input: words1 = ["amazon","apple","facebook","google","leetcode"], words2 = ["lc","eo"]
Output: ["leetcode"]
```

```text
Example 3
Input: words1 = ["acaac","cccbb","aacbb","caacc","bcbbb"], words2 = ["c","cc","b"]
Output: ["cccbb"]
```

## Constraints

- 1 <= words1.length, words2.length <= 10^4
- 1 <= words1[i].length, words2[i].length <= 10
- words1[i] and words2[i] consist only of lowercase English letters.
- All the strings of words1 are unique.

A word in words1 is universal when it contains every character in every words2 word with at least the required multiplicity. Return universal words in their original words1 order.
